title: feat(about): native libraries' licence notices in the Licences sheet
body:
**Priority:** P2. **Size:** L
**From:** #156 (decision of 2026-10-20: JavaScript packages in 2.0.0, native libraries here, in Stabilisation)

**The Licences sheet (#156) lists every JavaScript package Metro bundles. The binary also links native libraries that are not in that bundle and have no `node_modules` licence of their own, so the sheet does not show them yet.**

- **iOS** (from the podspecs in `node_modules`): SDWebImage and its WebP, SVG and AVIF coders, libavif, libdav1d, ReachabilitySwift.
- **React Native's native side:** Folly, boost, fmt, glog, double-conversion.
- **Android** (through Gradle): Glide, OkHttp, Fresco, AndroidX, Kotlin. Several are Apache-2.0, which also asks that a library's NOTICE file travel with it.

It is separate from #156 because the repo has no `ios/` or `android/` folders to read: EAS generates them at build time, so the native dependency list cannot come from Metro's source maps the way the JavaScript list does.

### Two routes to decide between

- **A. A hand-curated list with a drift check.** A committed `scripts/native-licences.json` with each library's licence and text, shown in the same sheet. `npm run check` scans the podspecs and `build.gradle` files in `node_modules` and fails on a native dependency the list does not name. About half a day of one-off work; it needs updating mostly on an Expo SDK bump (already a release decision); it catches direct native dependencies, not their transitive ones.
- **B. Generated at build time.** CocoaPods' acknowledgements and Google's `oss-licenses` plugin, wired in through config plugins. Exact, but every check of it costs an EAS build (Free quota), and Android shows Google's own licences screen rather than the app's sheet.

### Work

- [ ] The owner picks A or B.
- [ ] The chosen route, with the native libraries shown in About → Licences.
- [ ] `docs/license.md`: the "Native libraries — not yet listed" row says how the condition is met.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A store build shows the licence notice of every native library it links
- [ ] A new native dependency cannot reach a build unlisted without `npm run check` (or the build) saying so
- [ ] `npm run check` passes
why: The issue asks the owner to pick route A (a hand-curated list with a drift check) or B (generated at build time), and touches the licence notices (guardrail 2's asset-licensing rule): the skill asks.
